content:
anya: Follow-up from the attribute-handling RFC. We need a pragmatic path forward: full tenant partitioning vs gateway attr-eviction. Short takes?

mike: Eviction wins for cost and simplicity. Partitioning gives better per-tenant fidelity but multiplies ops.

tariq: We've seen issues when billing.customer_id gets evicted 
(incidents where charges were unknown). For hot tenants that matters.

lucy: Also noisy tenants with high-cardinality attrs blow up downstream queries. Dedicated partitions limit blast radius.

anya: Ops worry: partitioning increases number of streams/shards and complicates autoscaling. We must avoid per-tenant runaway cost.

mike: Proposed hybrid: keep a pinned minimal set of attributes at gateway, evict/trim others, and route the top-N noisy tenants to dedicated partitions.

tariq: Define "pinned" concretely. I propose: ["billing.customer_id", "billing.key", "tenant.id", "service.name", "env"]. Reject or flag events missing these at proto validation.

lucy: Add a "soft-missing" flag so we don't drop traces but mark them for operator attention. Makes debugging easier.

anya: Sample gateway config: 

```
eviction:
  pinned_attrs: ["billing.customer_id","tenant.id","service.name","env"]
  max_extra_attrs: 30
  missing_attr_policy: "flag"
routing:
  partition_threshold_tps: 1500
  dedicated_top_n: 20
```

mike: Routing key: tenant.id + billing.key. Cross-partition queries: we should support fanout+merge in the query layer for admin dashboards, but avoid it for low-latency SLO paths.

tariq: For the spike: I'll instrument a heuristic to detect noisy tenants (high attr cardinality or heavy cardinality growth) and route them to a dedicated stream.

ingest-bot: spike created by @anya: obs/ingest/eviction-partition-spike (https://phab.redwood/EVCT-214).

anya: Next actions: mike+tariq 3-day spike to implement pinned attr enforcement + soft-flagging, and prototype routing for top-20 noisy tenants. Lucy will craft a billing attribution eval set. I'll update RFC with the hybrid recommendation after we get spike numbers.

lucy: I'll run the evals and post false-negative rates for attribution.

mike: ack. posting progress here. :thumbsup:
